words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.ex: The diver submerge to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员潜水去探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid, especially water. If something submerges, it goes below the surface of a liquid.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.tr: v. 暂停；中止；延期； suspending
words.ex: The school will suspend the class due to snow.
words.ex_cn: 由于下雪，学校将暂停课程。
words.en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: He checks the calendar every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看日历。
words.en: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.ex: He was conscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后他醒了过来。
words.en: If you are conscious of something, you notice it or are aware of it.

words.ex: He gave a vicious smile before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前露出一个恶毒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vicious, you mean that they are violent and cruel, or that they are intended to cause someone great harm or suffering.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.ex: He immersed the cloth in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把布浸在水里。
words.en: To immerse something or someone means to put them into a liquid so that they are completely covered by it. It can also mean to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.ex: The army tried to invade the neighboring country.
words.ex_cn: 军队试图侵犯邻国。
words.en: To enter a country, town, or region by force in order to take control of it.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: Farmers irrigate their fields with water from the river.
words.ex_cn: 农民用河里的水灌溉他们的田地。
words.en: To supply land or crops with water by means of channels or pipes.

words.ex: His answer was apt for the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答对这个问题很恰当。
words.en: If someone is apt to do something, they often do it and so it is likely that they will do it again.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: n. 车辆；交通工具；媒介；
words.ex: The vehicle stopped at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在红灯前停了下来。
words.en: A vehicle is a machine such as a car, bus, or truck which has an engine and is used to carry people or goods from place to place.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.tr:
adj. 零下的；负的；
n. 缺点；
prep. 减去；
words.ex: The temperature is minus ten degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 气温是零下十摄氏度。
words.en: A minus is a mathematical symbol that represents subtraction or a negative quantity.

words.ex: He misunderstands the instructions.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了这些说明。
words.en: If you misunderstand someone or something, you do not understand them properly.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.tr:
n. 衣柜；壁橱；贮藏室
adj. 隐藏的
words.ex: He keeps his shirts in the closet.
words.ex_cn: 他把衬衫放在壁橱里。
words.en: A closet is a small room or space in a house or apartment where clothes, shoes, and other items are stored.

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: She took a glance at the clock.
words.ex_cn: 她瞥了一眼钟。
words.en: If you glance at something or someone, you look at them very quickly and then look away again immediately.

words.ex: He went to the dental clinic for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去牙科诊所做检查。
words.en: Relating to the teeth or to the work of a dentist.

words.tr: n. 娱乐；消遣；休闲活动
words.ex: Reading books is his favorite recreation.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: Recreation is activity that you do for enjoyment or amusement when you are not working.

words.tr:
n. 格式；
v. 格式化；
words.ex: The file is in PDF format.
words.ex_cn: 这个文件是PDF格式。
words.en: The way in which something is arranged or set out.

words.ex: The corporation sells smartphones worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司向全球销售智能手机。
words.en: A corporation is a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization.

words.ex: The word 'home' has a warm connotation.
words.ex_cn: ‘家’这个词有温暖的含义。
words.en: An idea or feeling that a word invokes in addition to its literal or primary meaning.

words.tr: n. 结构；布局；配置；外形
words.ex: The configuration of the computer is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑的配置非常简单。
words.en: The arrangement of parts or elements in a particular form, figure, or combination.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.ex: The dimension of the box is 10 cm by 5 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的尺寸是10厘米乘5厘米。
words.en: A dimension is a measurement of something in a particular direction, or the scope or scale of something.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: The stomach digests food into nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 胃将食物消化成营养物质。
words.en: To digest means to break down food in the stomach and intestines into substances that can be absorbed by the body. It can also mean to understand or assimilate information. As a noun, it refers to a compilation or summary of information.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The hostile neighbor shouted at us every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那个敌意的邻居每天早上都对我们大喊大叫。
words.en: If you are hostile to another person or an idea, you disagree with them or disapprove of them, often showing this in your behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.ex: The job position is still vacant.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位仍然空缺。
words.en: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.tr: adj. 发声的；嗓音的；直言不讳的；
words.ex: He made a vocal sound to get attention.
words.ex_cn: 他发出声音来引起注意。
words.en: If you are vocal about something, you express your opinions or feelings about it in a strong and public way.

words.tr:
n. 袭击；罢工；
v. 击打；侵袭；突然想到；
words.ex: The strike on the base happened at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 对基地的袭击发生在黎明时分。
words.en: To hit someone or something forcefully; to stop work as a form of protest.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显著的； v. 打击；“strike”的现在分词；
words.ex: The painting has a striking color scheme.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有着引人注目的配色。
words.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；最重要的；
n. 校长；负责人；
words.ex: The principal reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The person with the highest authority or most important position in an organization, institution, or group.

words.ex: He took his words in a literal sense.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的话按字面意思理解。
words.en: If you describe something as the literal truth or a literal fact, you are emphasizing that it is true.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: He got a vaccine last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周打了疫苗。
words.en: A vaccine is a substance containing a virus or bacterium in a form that is not harmful, given to a person or animal to prevent them from getting the disease that the virus or bacterium causes.

words.ex: His outlook on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的观点非常积极。
words.en: Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.ex: This plant is resistant to drought.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物对干旱有抵抗力。
words.en: If someone is resistant to something, they are opposed to it and want to prevent it.

words.ex: The teacher will inspect our homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会检查我们的作业。
words.en: If you inspect something, you look at it very carefully, usually in order to find out something about it.

words.ex: The spectator watched the game quietly.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者安静地观看了比赛。
words.en: A spectator is someone who watches an event, show, game, or activity.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.tr:
n. 弯曲；曲线；
v. （使）弯成弧形；
words.ex: The road has a sharp curve ahead.
words.ex_cn: 前面的路有一个急转弯。
words.en: A curve is a smooth, gradually bending line, for example part of the edge of a circle.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.tr:
n. 失败；
v. 击败；战胜；
words.ex: The team accepted the defeat with pride.
words.ex_cn: 球队以自豪的态度接受了失败。
words.en: If you defeat someone, you win a victory over them in a battle, game, or contest.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.ex: The teacher changed the parameter to make the test easier.
words.ex_cn: 老师更改了参数，使测试更容易。
words.en: A parameter is a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.ex: My ancestor came from China a hundred years ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先一百年前来自中国。
words.en: An ancestor is a person from whom one is descended, typically more remote than a grandparent.

words.ex: He spoke on behalf of his team.
words.ex_cn: 他代表他的团队发言。
words.en: If you do something on someone's behalf, you do it for that person as their representative.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.ex: Please don't disturb me while I'm reading.
words.ex_cn: 我读书时请不要打扰我。
words.en: To disturb someone means to interrupt what they are doing and cause them inconvenience or annoyance.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: He amended the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送信件之前修正了它。
words.en: To amend something means to make changes to it in order to improve it or make it more accurate.

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.ex: The passengers are aboard the plane.
words.ex_cn: 乘客们在飞机上。
words.en: On or onto a ship, aircraft, bus, or train.

words.tr:
n. 青少年；
adj. 青少年的；
words.ex: The adolescent walked to school with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个青少年和朋友们一起走路去上学。
words.en: An adolescent is a young person who is developing into an adult.

words.tr: n. 相互作用；相互影响；互动交流；
words.ex: The interaction between the two chemicals causes a reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质之间的相互作用引起反应。
words.en: An interaction is a situation where two or more people or things communicate with or react to each other.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.ex: The music accompanies the dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐伴随舞蹈。
words.en: To go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to play a musical accompaniment for.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He assists his brother with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助弟弟做作业。
words.en: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: He missed three consecutive days of school.
words.ex_cn: 他连续三天没上学。
words.en: Consecutive events, numbers, etc. follow one after another without an interruption.

words.ex: He won three successive championships.
words.ex_cn: 他连续赢得了三届冠军。
words.en: Following one after the other without interruption.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: A quiet room is conducive to studying.
words.ex_cn: 安静的房间有助于学习。
words.en: If one thing is conducive to another thing, it makes the other thing likely to happen.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: Farming is his main livelihood.
words.ex_cn: 务农是他的主要生计。
words.en: A person's livelihood is the way they earn money in order to live.

words.ex: The play ended in a tragedy when the hero died.
words.ex_cn: 当英雄去世时，这部戏剧以悲剧收场。
words.en: A tragedy is an extremely sad event or situation.

words.ex: The factory will automate the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将自动化装配线。
words.en: To automate a factory, office, or industrial process means to put in machines which can do the work instead of people.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.ex: Rare birds can be seen in this forest.
words.ex_cn: 这种森林里可以看到稀有的鸟类。
words.en: Something that is rare is not common and is therefore interesting or valuable.

words.ex: He lived in Paris for a decade.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎生活了十年。
words.en: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: The painter portrays a happy family in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这位画家在画中描绘了一个幸福的家庭。
words.en: To portray someone or something means to show or represent them in a painting, film, book, or other artistic work.

words.ex: He has a clear notion of right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他对对错有清晰的概念。
words.en: A notion is an idea or belief about something.

words.ex: The proportion of students who passed the test was high.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生比例很高。
words.en: A proportion is a part of a whole, or the relationship of one part to another in terms of size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.ex: The balloon will ascend into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 气球将升上天空。
words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.ex: He cannot breathe when he runs fast.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得快时无法呼吸。
words.en: To breathe means to take air into your lungs and then expel it, a process necessary for life.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: He is an architect who designs houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位设计房屋的建筑师。
words.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings and advises in their construction.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: He called an emergency doctor when he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到不舒服时，他叫了急诊医生。
words.en: An emergency is an unexpected and usually dangerous situation that calls for immediate action.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: He felt so sad that he thought about suicide.
words.ex_cn: 他感到非常难过，以至于想到了自杀。
words.en: Suicide is the act of deliberately killing oneself.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.ex: The accident was a serious incident.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是一起严重事件。
words.en: An incident is an event that is either unpleasant or unusual.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.ex: This segment of the book is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的这一部分非常有趣。
words.en: A segment of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: The toys are in the basement.
words.ex_cn: 玩具在地下室里。
words.en: The basement of a building is a room or area that is partly or completely below ground level.

words.tr:
n. 凡人
adj. 致命的；终有一死的
words.ex: All mortal beings must die someday.
words.ex_cn: 所有凡人都终有一死。
words.en: If you refer to the fact that people are mortal, you mean that they have to die and cannot live forever.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.ex: The boy resembles his father.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩长得像他父亲。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: He resolved the problem with a simple plan.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的计划解决了问题。
words.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

words.ex: He remarked that the weather was nice.
words.ex_cn: 他评论说天气很好。
words.en: If you remark that something is the case, you say that it is the case.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.ex: He will retire next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将退休。
words.en: If you retire, you stop working, usually because you have reached a certain age or because you are ill.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.ex: I asked for a refund after the product broke.
words.ex_cn: 产品坏了之后，我要求退款。
words.en: A refund is a sum of money that is returned to you, for example because you have paid too much or because you have returned goods to a shop.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.ex: The school is handling the affair carefully.
words.ex_cn: 学校正在小心处理这件事。
words.en: An affair is a situation or subject that is being dealt with or considered; it can also refer to a secret sexual relationship between two people.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: The actors rehearse their lines every evening.
words.ex_cn: 演员们每天晚上排练他们的台词。
words.en: To rehearse means to practice a play, piece of music, or other work for later public performance.

words.ex: He will renew his passport next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会更新他的护照。
words.en: To renew something means to begin it again or to make it new again.

words.tr: v. 使恢复精力；使复原；使变新
words.ex: A short nap can refresh you.
words.ex_cn: 小睡一会儿能让你恢复精力。
words.en: To refresh someone means to make them feel less tired or less hot.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.ex: He is allergic to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: If you are allergic to something, you become ill or get a rash when you eat it, smell it, or touch it.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: He lives in a tropical island near the equator.
words.ex_cn: 他住在赤道附近的一个热带岛屿上。
words.en: relating to or situated in or characteristic of the tropics (the region on either side of the equator)

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

words.tr: v. 使留下深刻印象；使铭记；
words.ex: His speech impressed everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲给在场的每个人留下了深刻印象。
words.en: If someone or something impresses you, you feel great admiration for them.

words.ex: The king oppresses the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王压迫穷人。
words.en: If someone oppresses people, they treat them cruelly or unfairly and prevent them from having the same rights as other people.

words.tr: v. 压下；降低；使沮丧；使不活泼；使萧条
words.ex: He depresses the button to start the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他按下按钮启动机器。
words.en: If something depresses you, it makes you feel sad and disappointed.

words.ex: The dove is a symbol of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: A symbol is a shape or design that is used to represent something such as an idea, a quality, or a process.

words.ex: He inherited his family's heritage.
words.ex_cn: 他继承了家族的遗产。
words.en: Heritage refers to the traditions, achievements, beliefs, etc., that are part of the history of a group or nation.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.ex: They settled in a small village after retirement.
words.ex_cn: 他们退休后在一个小村庄安顿下来。
words.en: To settle means to resolve or come to an agreement about a dispute, to establish a permanent home in a particular place, or to come to rest in a particular position.

words.ex: He dedicates his time to helping poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他致力于帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: If you dedicate yourself to something, you give all your attention and effort to it.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.tr: adj. 上瘾了的；入了迷的
words.ex: He is addicted to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他沉迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If you are addicted to something, you cannot stop doing it or using it, even though it may be harmful to you.

words.ex: He unfolded the map on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图在桌子上展开。
words.en: To open or spread out something that is folded; to develop or be revealed.

words.ex: The detective uncovered the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探揭开了真相。
words.en: To uncover something means to remove the cover from it or to reveal it by investigation or inquiry.

words.ex: The storm unleashed heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 风暴释放出大雨。
words.en: If you say that someone or something unleashes a powerful force, feeling, activity, or group, you mean that they suddenly start it or send it to move somewhere.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.ex: The country expanded its territory after the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在战争后扩大了它的领土。
words.en: An area of land that is controlled by a particular country, ruler, or military force.

words.ex: The teacher will classify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师将按年龄对学生进行分类。
words.en: To classify things means to divide them into groups or types so that things with similar characteristics are in the same group.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.tr:
adj. 手工的；体力的；
n. 说明书；
words.ex: He made a manual copy of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他手工抄写了一封信。
words.en: A manual is a book which tells you how to do something or how a piece of machinery works.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；自由主义的；
n. 自由党党员；
words.ex: He is a liberal teacher who listens to students.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，会倾听学生的声音。
words.en: A liberal person, system, or policy is one that is in favour of allowing people a lot of freedom in their behaviour or opinions.

words.ex: They will liberate the prisoners tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天会释放这些囚犯。
words.en: To liberate a place or the people in it means to free them from the political or military control of another country, area, or group of people.

words.tr: n. 养老金；退休金；抚恤金；
words.ex: He receives a monthly pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后每月领取养老金。
words.en: A pension is a sum of money which a retired, widowed, or disabled person regularly receives from the state or from a former employer.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: The store sells cheap merchandise.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售廉价商品。
words.en: Goods to be bought and sold.

words.ex: The merchant sells fresh fruit every morning.
words.ex_cn: 商人每天早上卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A merchant is a person who buys and sells goods, especially one who owns a shop.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.ex: The violent storm destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场暴力的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If someone is violent, or if they do something that is violent, they use physical force or weapons to hurt, injure, or kill other people.

words.ex: The glass is transparent.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃是透明的。
words.en: If something is transparent, you can see through it.

words.ex: It is apparent that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is apparent, it seems to be true, although you cannot be certain that it is.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: adj. 值得…的；值得尊敬的；
words.ex: This book is worthy of reading.
words.ex_cn: 这本书值得读。
words.en: If something or someone is worthy of something, they deserve it because they have the qualities or abilities required.

words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.ex: He screamed in agony after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后痛苦地大叫。
words.en: Agony is very severe physical or mental pain.

words.ex: He shouted with fury when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他输掉比赛时，他愤怒地大喊。
words.en: Fury is a feeling of intense anger.

words.ex: Align your goals with your actions.
words.ex_cn: 让你的目标与行动保持一致。
words.en: To arrange something in a straight line or in the correct position in relation to something else, usually so that it is parallel to it.

words.ex: They booked a hotel suite for their honeymoon.
words.ex_cn: 他们为蜜月预订了一间酒店套房。
words.en: A set of rooms designated for use together, especially in a hotel; a set of musical compositions designed to be performed in a sequence.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.tr:
adj. 联合的；共同的；
n. 关节；接合处；
words.ex: They signed a joint agreement to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一项联合协议来保护环境。
words.en: A joint is a place where two things are joined together, especially the place where two bones are connected in a person's or animal's body.

words.ex: You must concentrate on your homework.
words.ex_cn: 你必须集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you concentrate on something, you give it your full attention and think about it carefully.

words.tr:
n. 崇拜；崇敬；礼拜；
v. 崇拜；尊崇；做礼拜；
words.ex: The ancient people showed worship to the sun.
words.ex_cn: 古人对太阳进行崇拜。
words.en: The feeling or expression of reverence and adoration for a deity.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.ex: I like coffee, and she likes it likewise.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢咖啡，她也喜欢。
words.en: You use likewise when you are comparing two methods, states, or situations and saying that they are similar.

words.ex: The teacher will announce the results tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天将宣布结果。
words.en: To announce something means to make it known publicly or officially.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.tr: v. 喷射；喷出；驱逐；逐出
words.ex: The volcano ejects lava during an eruption.
words.ex_cn: 火山在喷发时喷出岩浆。
words.en: If you eject someone or something from a place, you force them to leave.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.ex: They erect a flagpole in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们在公园里竖立一根旗杆。
words.en: If people erect something such as a building, bridge, or barrier, they build it or create it.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.ex: The rule excludes children under 12.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则排除了12岁以下的孩子。
words.en: To exclude someone or something means to prevent them from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 马具；
words.ex: We must harness the power of the sun.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须利用太阳的能量。
words.en: A harness is a set of straps which fit under a person's arms and fasten round their body in order to keep a piece of equipment in place or to prevent the person moving from a place.

words.ex: There is a pile of books on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上有一堆书。
words.en: A pile of things is a quantity of them lying on top of one another. If you pile things somewhere, you put them there so that they form a pile.

words.ex: He took a pill for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒药丸来缓解头痛。
words.en: A pill is a small solid mass of medicine that you swallow whole.

words.ex: He found a piece of metal in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里发现了一块金属。
words.en: Metal is a hard, shiny substance such as iron, gold, or steel.

words.ex: I checked the class schedule for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我查看了明天的课程时间表。
words.en: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

words.ex: The theft of the bike was reported to the police.
words.ex_cn: 这起自行车被盗事件已向警方报告。
words.en: Theft is the act of stealing.

words.ex: The drought made it hard to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 旱灾使种植庄稼变得困难。
words.en: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls and hence there is a shortage of water.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: The church has a big dome above the altar.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的祭坛上方有一个大穹顶。
words.en: A dome is a rounded vault made of either curved segments or a shell of revolution, meaning an arch rotated around its central vertical axis.

words.ex: She showed compassion for the homeless man.
words.ex_cn: 她对那个无家可归的人表示同情。
words.en: Compassion is a feeling of pity, sympathy, and understanding for someone who is suffering.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.ex: He walked home with his companion.
words.ex_cn: 他和同伴一起走回家。
words.en: A companion is someone who you spend time with or who you are travelling with.

words.ex: He composes music in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间创作音乐。
words.en: To compose something means to make it by combining parts or elements.

words.ex: Small commerce helps local towns grow.
words.ex_cn: 小商业有助于小镇的发展。
words.en: Commerce is the activity of buying and selling things, especially on a large scale.

words.tr:
adj. 贸易的；商业的；
n. 广告；
words.ex: The commercial ship sailed to another country.
words.ex_cn: 这艘贸易船只驶向了另一个国家。
words.en: Commercial relates to the business of buying and selling goods and services.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.tr:
v. 建造；构造；
n. 概念；
words.ex: They construct houses with bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他们用砖块建造房屋。
words.en: To construct something means to build or create it, usually something large such as a building, road, or machine.

words.ex: The soldiers defend their country from enemies.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们保卫自己的国家免受敌人入侵。
words.en: To defend means to protect someone or something from attack, harm, or criticism. It can also involve arguing in support of someone or something.

words.ex: The train will derail if the tracks are broken.
words.ex_cn: 如果铁轨损坏，火车就会脱轨。
words.en: To cause a train or other vehicle to leave its tracks accidentally; to divert or cause to deviate from an intended course.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: He denies taking the money.
words.ex_cn: 他否认拿了钱。
words.en: To deny means to declare that something is not true, or to refuse to give or grant something.

words.ex: He devotes his time to helping children.
words.ex_cn: 他投入时间帮助孩子们。
words.en: If you devote yourself, your time, or your energy to something, you spend all or most of your time or energy on it.

words.ex: The doctor checked his daily intake of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他每天的糖摄入量。
words.en: The process of taking something in, especially food, air, or information.

words.tr: adj. 顺利的；宽裕的；有钱的
words.ex: He comes from a well-off family and never worries about money.
words.ex_cn: 他来自一个顺利的家庭，从不为钱发愁。
words.en: Someone who is well-off is rich enough to be able to do and buy most of the things that they want.

words.ex: He bought a second-hand bike for $20.
words.ex_cn: 他花20美元买了一辆二手自行车。
words.en: used, owned, or worn by someone else before; not new.

words.ex: At the outset, he was unsure about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 在开始时，他对这个计划并不确定。
words.en: The outset of something is the beginning of it.

words.ex: He had a setback when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，遇到了挫折。
words.en: A setback is an event that delays your progress or reverses some of the progress that you have made.

words.ex: The invention of the wheel was a landmark in human history.
words.ex_cn: 轮子的发明是人类历史上的一个里程碑。
words.en: A landmark is a building or feature of a landscape that is easily seen and recognized from a distance, especially one that enables someone to establish their location.

words.ex: Graduating from high school was a big milestone for him.
words.ex_cn: 从高中毕业对他来说是一个重要的事件。
words.en: A milestone is a significant event or stage in the development of something.

words.ex: He filed a lawsuit against the company.
words.ex_cn: 他向这家公司提起了诉讼。
words.en: A lawsuit is a case in a court of law which concerns a dispute between two people or organizations.

words.tr: n. 营业额；人员流动率；周转率；
words.ex: The store's turnover increased last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店上个月的营业额增加了。
words.en: The amount of money taken by a business in a particular period.

words.ex: The dogs had three offspring last spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些狗去年春天生了三只幼崽。
words.en: Someone's offspring are their children.

words.ex: The instructions were straightforward and easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很简单，容易遵循。
words.en: If you describe something as straightforward, you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周不得不接受手术。
words.en: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you or is done to you.

words.tr:
n. 勒索；敲诈
v. 勒索；讹诈
words.ex: He threatened to tell the truth unless she paid him money — that's blackmail.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁说，除非她付钱，否则就说出真相——这就是敲诈。
words.en: Blackmail is the action of threatening to reveal a secret about someone, unless they do something you want, such as give you money.

words.ex: Please tell me beforehand if you can't come.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不能来，请提前告诉我。
words.en: If you do something beforehand, you do it earlier than a particular event.

words.tr: n. 崩溃；故障；细目分类；
words.ex: The stress led to a breakdown.
words.ex_cn: 压力导致了崩溃。
words.en: A breakdown is a failure of a system, machine, or relationship, or a sudden collapse in someone's mental health.

words.tr:
n. 旁路；
v. 绕过；
words.ex: The city built a bypass around the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市建了一条绕过老城区的旁路。
words.en: If you bypass a place or a system, you avoid it or go around it instead of going through it.

words.ex: He became a dropout after failing math class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试不及格后退学了。
words.en: A dropout is a person who leaves school or college before they have finished their studies, especially because they are not interested in continuing.

words.tr: n. 解雇；活动停止期间
words.ex: He got a layoff last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月被裁员了。
words.en: A layoff is the termination of employment of an employee or, more commonly, a group of employees for business reasons, such as the decision of the company to downsize its operations.

words.ex: He bought a brand-new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆全新的自行车。
words.en: Completely new, as if recently made or acquired.

words.ex: He dwells in a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一所小房子里。
words.en: If you dwell on something, especially something unpleasant, you think, speak, or write about it a lot or for quite a long time.

words.ex: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 骑士举起盾牌来挡箭。
words.en: A shield is a piece of armor held in the hand or worn on the arm to protect the body from missiles or blows. It can also refer to something that protects or defends someone or something from harm or danger.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.ex: The small room was cosy with a warm blanket and a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间铺着温暖的毯子，喝着热茶，非常舒适。
words.en: A place or situation that is cosy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: The bang woke me up at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 那声巨响在午夜把我吵醒了。
words.en: A bang is a sudden loud noise such as the noise of an explosion.

words.tr: v. 自夸；夸耀；自豪地拥有
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他夸耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, in a way that other people may find irritating or offensive.

words.ex: The river forms the border between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 这条河是两个国家的边界。
words.en: The edge or boundary of something, or the part near it; a dividing line.

words.ex: He is chewing gum loudly.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大声地嚼口香糖。
words.en: To chew means to bite and grind food in your mouth so it becomes soft enough to swallow.

words.ex: The police found a clue at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了一条线索。
words.en: A clue is an object or piece of information that helps to solve a problem or mystery.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.ex: The children are eager to open their presents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们渴望打开他们的礼物。
words.en: If you are eager to do or have something, you want to do or have it very much.

words.tr:
v. 领会；抓紧；
n. 领会；
words.ex: I couldn't grasp the meaning of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 我没能领会这首诗的含义。
words.en: To grasp something means to take it in your hand and hold it firmly.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.tr:
n. 紧握；掌握；控制；
v. 紧握；掌握；
words.ex: He has a strong grip on the handle.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧握住把手。
words.en: To grip something means to hold it tightly. It can also mean to hold someone's attention completely.

words.tr: v. 劈砍；侵入（计算机等）
words.ex: He hacked the tree with an axe.
words.ex_cn: 他用斧头劈砍那棵树。
words.en: To hack means to cut or chop something with rough or heavy blows, or to gain unauthorized access to data in a system or computer.

words.tr: adj. 整洁的；整齐的；有条理的
words.ex: He keeps his desk neat.
words.ex_cn: 他保持书桌整洁。
words.en: Neat things are tidy, smart, or carefully arranged.

words.ex: The palm tree grows near the beach.
words.ex_cn: 棕榈树长在海滩附近。
words.en: The inner surface of the hand that extends from the wrist to the base of the fingers; also refers to the tropical tree with large divided leaves.

words.tr: adj. 锋利的；骤变的；灵敏的；尖刻的；
words.ex: The knife is sharp enough to cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀足够锋利，可以切纸。
words.en: Having a thin edge or a fine point that is capable of cutting or piercing; keen.

words.ex: He became famous for his music and gained great fame.
words.ex_cn: 他因音乐而闻名，获得了巨大的名声。
words.en: the state of being known or talked about by many people, especially on account of notable achievements

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: His answer was vague and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不明确，难以理解。
words.en: If something written or spoken is vague, it does not explain or express things clearly.

words.tr:
n. 车费；费用；
v. 进展；成功（或不成功等）；
words.ex: The bus fare is two dollars.
words.ex_cn: 公交车费是两美元。
words.en: The fare is the amount of money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.

words.ex: He opted to stay home instead of going out.
words.ex_cn: 他选择待在家里而不是出去。
words.en: If you opt for something, or opt to do something, you choose it or decide to do it in preference to anything else.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a small dose of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一小剂量的药。
words.en: A dose of a medicine or a drug is the amount of it that you take at one time, or the amount that is recommended for you to take.

words.ex: He made a pledge to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了帮助穷人的保证。
words.en: A pledge is a serious promise or agreement, especially one made publicly or officially. It can also refer to something given as security for the fulfillment of a contract or the payment of a debt.

words.ex: The wood surface is rough.
words.ex_cn: 木头表面很粗糙。
words.en: If a surface is rough, it is not smooth and has bumps or uneven areas.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.ex: The wind scatter the leaves everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得四处分散。
words.en: To scatter means to throw or drop things over a wide area in an irregular way, or to cause a group of people or animals to move apart in different directions.

words.ex: The pond is shallow, so you can see the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这个池塘很浅，所以你能看到底部。
words.en: If something is shallow, it does not extend far down from the top surface.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.tr:
n. 幻灯片；滑梯；
v. （使）滑动；下滑；
words.ex: He showed a slide of his vacation photos.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了一张他度假照片的幻灯片。
words.en: To move smoothly along a surface while maintaining continuous contact with it; to pass or move quietly or smoothly; a structure with a smooth sloping surface for children to slide down; a decline from a higher to a lower level or status.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr:
v. 伸展；延伸；持续；
n. 一段；伸展；
words.ex: He stretches his arms every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上伸展手臂。
words.en: To stretch is to extend your body or a part of your body to its full length, or to extend something else to its full length or beyond its normal limits.

words.tr:
n. 摇摆；
v. 摇摆；
words.ex: The child enjoyed the swing at the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子喜欢在公园里荡秋千。
words.en: If something swings or if you swing it, it moves repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side from a fixed point. If you swing somewhere, you move there by holding onto something and moving your body through the air.

words.ex: The doctor examined the tissue under a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 医生在显微镜下检查了组织。
words.en: Tissue is a group of cells that have a similar structure and that work together to perform a specific function.

words.tr:
n. 哭泣；落泪
v. 流泪；流出
words.ex: Her weep lasted for hours after the news.
words.ex_cn: 听到消息后，她的哭泣持续了数小时。
words.en: To shed tears, especially as an expression of distress or pain.

words.ex: The farmer dug a ditch to water the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农夫挖了一条沟来给田地浇水。
words.en: A ditch is a long narrow trench or furrow dug in the ground, especially for drainage or irrigation.

words.tr:
n. （鸟或羊）群；（人）群；
v. 聚集；群集；
words.ex: A flock of birds flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过田野。
words.en: A flock is a group of birds, sheep, or goats, or a large group of people. It can also refer to a soft material for stuffing cushions, quilts, etc., made from wool or cotton. As a verb, it means to gather or move in a flock.

words.ex: He drew a loop with the pencil.
words.ex_cn: 他用铅笔画了一个圈。
words.en: A loop is a shape produced by a curve that bends round and crosses itself, or a piece of wire, string, etc. that has this shape. It can also refer to a repeated sequence of operations or events in a computer program or in a process.

words.tr: v. 恳求；辩护；答辩；以…为理由
words.ex: He pleaded for help when he was lost.
words.ex_cn: 当他迷路时，他恳求帮助。
words.en: If you plead with someone to do something, you ask them in an intense, emotional way to do it.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.ex: The cruel king punished the innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 残酷的国王惩罚了无辜的人。
words.en: Someone who is cruel deliberately causes pain or distress to others or feels no concern about it.

words.tr:
n. 洗涤槽；水槽；
v. （使）沉没；
words.ex: The dirty dishes are in the sink.
words.ex_cn: 脏盘子在水槽里。
words.en: If a boat sinks, or if something sinks it, it disappears below the surface of a mass of water.

words.ex: He crossed the threshold of adulthood at 18.
words.ex_cn: 他在18岁时进入了成年的起始点。
words.en: The threshold of something is the point at which it begins or changes.

words.ex: The flowers wither in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下枯萎。
words.en: If a plant withers, it dries up and dies. If something withers, it becomes weaker or less important until it disappears completely.

words.tr:
v. 使目眩；使眼花；使惊叹
n. 耀眼；眩惑；灿烂
words.ex: The stars dazzle at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的星星闪耀夺目。
words.en: If something dazzles you, it is so bright that you cannot see properly for a short time. It can also mean to greatly impress someone.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.ex: The hurricane destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 飓风摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A hurricane is an extremely violent wind or storm.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.ex: The blind man walks with a white cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位失明的男人用白色手杖走路。
words.en: Unable to see; lacking the sense of sight.

words.ex: She blends flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To mix substances together so that they combine into a single substance.

words.ex: The rope is slack and hangs loosely.
words.ex_cn: 绳子是松弛的，垂挂着。
words.en: If something is slack, it is loose and not firmly stretched or tightly in position. It can also describe a period of low activity or a lack of effort in work or activity.

words.ex: The swamp is full of tall grass and frogs.
words.ex_cn: 这个沼泽里长满了高草和青蛙。
words.en: A swamp is an area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: Italian cuisine is famous for pasta and pizza.
words.ex_cn: 意大利烹调风格以意大利面和披萨闻名。
words.en: A style or method of cooking, especially as characteristic of a particular country, region, or establishment.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.ex: The wedding ceremony was beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼仪式很美丽。
words.en: A ceremony is a formal event held on special occasions such as weddings, graduations, or official functions, often involving traditional or religious rituals.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 巨大的；大量的；辽阔的；
words.ex: The desert is vast and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠巨大而空旷。
words.en: If you describe something as vast, you mean that it is very large.

words.tr:
n. 全体演员；
v. 投掷；扔；投射；
words.ex: The cast of the play performed very well.
words.ex_cn: 这部剧的全体演员表演得非常好。
words.en: To cast something means to throw it forcefully in a particular direction.

words.ex: The cake has a sweet flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有一种甜味。
words.en: The flavor of a food or drink is its taste, especially a pleasant or distinctive one.

words.ex: Parents often spoil their children with too many toys.
words.ex_cn: 父母经常用太多玩具宠坏孩子。
words.en: To spoil something means to reduce its quality or value, often by damaging it in some way. It can also mean to treat someone, especially a child, with too much kindness or indulgence, leading to their detriment.

words.tr:
adj. 唯一的；
n. 鞋底；
words.ex: He is the sole owner of the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家商店唯一的主人。
words.en: If you describe something as the sole thing of a particular kind, you mean that it is the only one of that kind.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He had a stumble on the rocky path.
words.ex_cn: 他在布满石头的小路上绊了一跤。
words.en: To stumble means to trip or momentarily lose one's balance while walking or running. It can also refer to speaking in a hesitant or faltering manner.

words.tr: adj. 秃头的；不加修饰的；赤裸裸的
words.ex: The old man is bald.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是秃头的。
words.en: Someone who is bald has little or no hair on the top of their head.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: He picked up a brochure about the city.
words.ex_cn: 他拿了一本关于这座城市的宣传小册子。
words.en: A brochure is a type of small magazine or booklet containing pictures and information about something or advertising something.

words.ex: He knows good etiquette at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他知道晚餐时的礼貌规矩。
words.en: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.ex: He analyzes data every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天分析数据。
words.en: To examine something methodically and in detail, typically in order to explain and interpret it.

words.ex: The judge made a fair decision to show justice.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了公正的裁决以体现公正。
words.en: Justice is fairness in the way that people are treated.

words.ex: He will alter the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会改动计划。
words.en: To alter something means to change it, usually slightly, or to cause the characteristics of something to change.

words.tr:
n. 文件；公文；文献；
v. 记录；为…提供证明；
words.ex: He submitted the document to the office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件提交给了办公室。
words.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

words.ex: He wrote a memorandum about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份关于会议的备忘录。
words.en: A memorandum is a written proposal or reminder, especially in a business context.

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

words.ex: The planet Mars is red.
words.ex_cn: 火星是红色的。
words.en: A planet is a large object in space that moves around a star, such as the sun, and does not produce its own light.

words.ex: His mission is to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他的使命是帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A mission is an important task that people are given to do, especially one that involves travelling to another country.

words.ex: The army conquered the small city after a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 军队经过长期战斗征服了这座小城。
words.en: To conquer means to take control of a country or city and its people by force, or to successfully deal with or control something.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.tr:
n. 塑料；
adj. 塑料的；
words.ex: The bottle is made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子是塑料做的。
words.en: A plastic is a material which is produced from oil by a chemical process and which is used to make many objects. It is light in weight and does not break easily.

words.ex: She buys organic vegetables at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买有机蔬菜。
words.en: Relating to or derived from living matter; denoting or characterized by a harmonious relationship between the elements of a whole.

words.tr:
v. 见证；
n. 证人；目击者；
words.ex: He witnessed the accident yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天目睹了那起事故。
words.en: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident. Witnesses are often called upon to give evidence in court.

words.tr: n. 平板电脑；（刻有文字的）匾；
words.ex: He uses a tablet to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他用平板电脑读书。
words.en: A tablet is a small, flat computer that is controlled by touching the screen. It can also refer to a small, solid piece of medicine that you swallow.

words.ex: The Earth is divided into two hemispheres: north and south.
words.ex_cn: 地球被分为两个半球：北半球和南半球。
words.en: A hemisphere is one half of the earth, especially the northern or southern half above or below the equator, or the eastern or western half.

words.ex: The company used a new formula to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 公司使用了一个新方案来解决问题。
words.en: A formula is a plan or method that is used to achieve a particular goal, especially in science or mathematics.

words.ex: The room was in complete disorder.
words.ex_cn: 房间一片混乱。
words.en: A disorder is a state of confusion or untidiness, or a medical problem that affects the mind or body.

words.ex: He tried acupuncture to relieve his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他尝试针刺疗法来缓解背痛。
words.en: Acupuncture is a form of treatment that involves inserting very thin needles through a person's skin at specific points on the body, to various depths, for therapeutic purposes.

words.tr: n. 雕刻（术）；雕塑品；雕刻品；
words.ex: He made a beautiful sculpture from clay.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏土做了一件精美的雕刻。
words.en: Sculpture is the art of making two- or three-dimensional representative or abstract forms, especially by carving stone or wood or by casting metal or plaster.

words.ex: He went to school despite the rain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管下雨，他还是去上学了。
words.en: Without being affected by; in spite of.

words.tr:
n. 推迟；延缓；耽搁；
v. 推迟；延缓；耽搁；
words.ex: The flight had a delay because of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 由于风暴，航班推迟了。
words.en: If you delay doing something, you do not do it immediately or at the planned or expected time, but you leave it until later.

words.ex: The solar panel collects energy from the sun.
words.ex_cn: 太阳能板从太阳收集能量。
words.en: Solar means relating to the sun or using the energy from the sun to produce electricity.

words.ex: The teacher will determine the winner of the contest.
words.ex_cn: 老师将确定比赛的获胜者。
words.en: If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.

words.ex: The parliament passed a new law about education.
words.ex_cn: 国会通过了一项关于教育的新法律。
words.en: A parliament is a legislative body of government, typically composed of elected representatives, that is responsible for making laws and representing the interests of the people.

words.ex: The satellite sends pictures from space.
words.ex_cn: 卫星从太空发送图片。
words.en: A satellite is an object which has been sent into space in order to collect information or to be part of a communications system. Satellites move continually round the earth or around another planet.

words.ex: The coastal village has beautiful beaches.
words.ex_cn: 这个沿海村庄有美丽的海滩。
words.en: relating to the coast, the area where the land meets the sea

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: I recognize her face from school.
words.ex_cn: 我从学校认出了她的脸。
words.en: If you recognize someone or something, you know who or what they are because you have seen or heard them before.

words.tr: v. 设置；放；“set”的现在分词； n. 环境；背景；
words.ex: He is setting the alarm for 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把闹钟设置为早上6点。
words.en: The context and environment in which something is set or takes place.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；给书籍、杂志等加插图；
words.ex: The teacher illustrated the point with a simple story.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的故事来举例说明这个观点。
words.en: To illustrate something means to explain or demonstrate it clearly, often by giving examples or by using pictures or diagrams.

words.ex: The dark clouds indicate rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云表明要下雨了。
words.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

words.ex: We celebrate my birthday with cake and friends.
words.ex_cn: 我们用蛋糕和朋友庆祝我的生日。
words.en: To celebrate means to mark a special day, event, or occasion with festivities or ceremonies. It can also mean to praise or honor someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 评论；表达意见；
n. 评论；意见；
words.ex: He commented on the movie last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚对这部电影发表了评论。
words.en: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it.

words.ex: The children loved the circus with clowns and elephants.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢有小丑和大象的马戏团。
words.en: A circus is a group of performers that include clowns, acrobats, and trained animals, who travel to different places to entertain people.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.ex: The scientist created a clone of the sheep.
words.ex_cn: 科学家克隆了一只羊。
words.en: A clone is an organism or cell produced asexually from one ancestor or stock, to which they are genetically identical.

words.ex: He has a high fever as a symptom of the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧是流感的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.ex: The tenant pays rent every month.
words.ex_cn: 房客每个月支付租金。
words.en: A tenant is a person who rents land or property from a landlord.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
