words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.tr: prep. 关于； v. 看待；“regard”的现在分词；
words.ex: He sent me an email regarding the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给我发了一封关于会议的邮件。
words.en: You can use regarding to indicate the subject that is being talked or written about.

words.ex: He is an undergraduate at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的一名本科生。
words.en: An undergraduate is a student at a university or college who is studying for their first degree.

words.ex: He stayed home because he had the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他因为得了流感待在家里。
words.en: The flu is an infectious disease characterized by fever, aches and pains, and respiratory symptoms.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

words.ex: He wants to study psychology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学学习心理学。
words.en: Psychology is the scientific study of the human mind and the reasons for people's behaviour.

words.ex: He likes to study physics in school.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在学校学习物理。
words.en: Physics is the scientific study of matter, energy, force, and motion, and how they relate to each other.

words.ex: He likes biology because it teaches about animals and plants.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢生物学，因为它教关于动物和植物的知识。
words.en: Biology is the science which is concerned with the study of living things.

words.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.
words.ex_cn: 她为了这个特殊场合穿了一条裙子。
words.en: An occasion is a particular time when something happens, or a special event.

words.tr:
n. 反面；对立面；
adj. 对面的；
prep. 与…相对；
words.ex: The opposite of black is white.
words.ex_cn: 黑色的反面是白色。
words.en: If one thing is opposite another, it is on the other side of a space from it.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.tr: n. 受公众注意的程度；简介；轮廓；
words.ex: The celebrity's profile rose after the TV interview.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人经过电视采访后，受公众注意的程度提高了。
words.en: A profile is a side view of something, especially a person's face, or a brief description of someone or something.

words.ex: He paid off his debt last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月还清了债务。
words.en: A debt is a sum of money that you owe someone.

words.tr:
adj. 壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的；总的；
n. 大钢琴；
words.ex: The grand castle stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 壮丽的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: If you describe a building or a piece of scenery as grand, you mean that its size or appearance is very impressive.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.ex: The community cleaned the park together.
words.ex_cn: 社区居民一起清理了公园。
words.en: A community is a group of people who live in the same area or who have the same interests, religion, or nationality.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人建造了金字塔。
words.en: Belonging to the very distant past and no longer in existence.

words.ex: The doctor gave me antibiotics for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗生素来治疗感染。
words.en: Antibiotics are medicines that are used to treat infections caused by bacteria.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: The air feels humid after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 雨后空气感觉湿润。
words.en: You use humid to describe an atmosphere or climate that is very damp, and usually very hot.

words.ex: There is a five-minute interval between the two classes.
words.ex_cn: 两节课之间有五分钟的间隔。
words.en: An interval is a period of time between two events or dates.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr:
adv. 顺时针方向地
adj. 顺时针方向的
words.ex: Turn the knob clockwise to open the jar.
words.ex_cn: 顺时针转动旋钮来打开罐子。
words.en: Moving in the same direction as the hands of a clock.

words.ex: He is an intermediate student in English.
words.ex_cn: 他是英语的中级学生。
words.en: An intermediate stage, level, or position is one that occurs between two other stages, levels, or positions.

words.tr: n. 生物体；有机体；有机组织；
words.ex: A bacterium is a simple organism.
words.ex_cn: 细菌是一种简单的生物体。
words.en: An organism is a living thing that has an organized structure, can react to stimuli, reproduce, grow, adapt, and maintain homeostasis.

words.tr: n. 寄生虫；寄生生物；依赖他人过活者；
words.ex: The parasite lives inside the host's body.
words.ex_cn: 这种寄生虫生活在宿主的体内。
words.en: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host organism and gets its food from or at the expense of its host.

words.ex: The desert has little vegetation.
words.ex_cn: 这个沙漠植被很少。
words.en: Vegetation refers to plants in general, or the plants that are found in a particular area. It can also refer to a life that is dull or inactive, often due to illness or lack of exercise.

words.tr:
n. （果树的）花朵；
v. 开花；
words.ex: The apple tree is full of blossom in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，苹果树上开满了花。
words.en: When a tree or plant blossoms, it produces flowers before producing fruit that can be eaten.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.ex: Each student received their respective book.
words.ex_cn: 每个学生都收到了他们各自的书。
words.en: Relating or belonging separately to each of two or more people or things.

words.ex: He is always punctual for class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课总是准时。
words.en: If you are punctual, you do something or arrive somewhere at the right time and are not late.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.ex: The tree grows in a vertical line.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树垂直生长。
words.en: Something that is vertical stands or points straight up.

words.ex: This jacket is waterproof.
words.ex_cn: 这件夹克是防水的。
words.en: Something that is waterproof does not let water pass through it.

words.ex: He made an abrupt stop at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 他在红灯前突然停了下来。
words.en: If something happens abruptly, it happens suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.ex: The table is made of a composite material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由一种合成材料制成的。
words.en: A composite is something that is made up of several different parts or materials.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.tr: v. （使）停滞；不发展；因不流动而变得污浊
words.ex: The economy began to stagnate after the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 经济在危机后开始停滞。
words.en: If something such as a business or project stagnates, it stops developing or making progress.

words.tr: v. 占主导地位；占支配地位；
words.ex: English predominate in this region.
words.ex_cn: 英语在这个地区占主导地位。
words.en: If one type of person or thing predominates in a group, there is more of that type than of any other.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；
words.ex: This result is noteworthy because it changes our understanding.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果值得注意，因为它改变了我们的理解。
words.en: If you describe something as noteworthy, you mean that it is interesting, significant, or important enough to deserve attention or to be noticed.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: Asia is the largest continent.
words.ex_cn: 亚洲是最大的洲。
words.en: A continent is a very large area of land, such as Africa or Asia, that consists of several countries.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.ex: He bought a new device to take photos.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新设备来拍照。
words.en: A device is an object or machine that has been invented for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.tr: n. 代表大会；议会；国会；
words.ex: The congress met to discuss new laws.
words.ex_cn: 代表大会召开以讨论新法律。
words.en: A congress is a formal meeting of representatives, as of various nations, to discuss problems or to make decisions.

words.ex: The coach changed his tactic to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了战术以赢得比赛。
words.en: A tactic is a method or plan chosen to bring about a desired future, such as achieving a goal or solving a problem.

words.tr: adj. 大都市的；大城市的；
words.ex: He lives in a metropolitan city like New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约这样的大都市。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a metropolis or large city, especially as the main city of a country or region.

words.tr:
n. 救援；营救；
v. 救援；营救；
words.ex: The rescue came just in time to save the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 救援及时赶到，救出了徒步者。
words.en: To rescue someone or something means to save them from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

words.ex: The weather bureau issued a storm warning.
words.ex_cn: 气象局发布了风暴预警。
words.en: A bureau is an office, organization, or government department that collects and distributes information.

words.tr:
n. 最大限度；最大量；
adj. 最大极限的；最多的；
words.ex: The maximum of the crowd is 100 people.
words.ex_cn: 人群的上限是100人。
words.en: The greatest or highest amount possible or attained.

words.ex: He copes with stress by walking every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天散步来应对压力。
words.en: To cope with a problem or task means to deal with it successfully.

words.ex: We took a different route to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们换了条路线以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A route is a way from one place to another, or the path that something follows to reach a destination.

words.tr: adj. 未加工处理过的；生的；
words.ex: He eats raw vegetables every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吃未加工的蔬菜。
words.en: Raw refers to something that is in its natural state and not processed or cooked.

words.ex: The bread is stale because it was left out too long.
words.ex_cn: 面包不新鲜了，因为它放得太久。
words.en: If food or air is stale, it is no longer fresh and therefore unpleasant.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians built pyramids for their kings.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人为他们的国王建造了金字塔。
words.en: A pyramid is a monumental structure with a square or triangular base and sloping sides that meet in a point at the top, especially one built of stone as a royal tomb in ancient Egypt.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: The ratio of boys to girls is 3 to 2.
words.ex_cn: 男孩与女孩的比例是3比2。
words.en: A ratio is a relationship between two numbers indicating how many times the first number contains the second.

words.ex: The rhythm of the music made everyone dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐的节奏让所有人都跳起了舞。
words.en: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

words.ex: Open the window to ventilate the room.
words.ex_cn: 打开窗户给房间通风。
words.en: To ventilate means to cause fresh air to enter and move around a room, building, etc., or to express your opinions or feelings about something openly.

words.ex: The car's velocity increased on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在高速公路上的速度增加了。
words.en: Velocity is the speed at which something moves in a particular direction.

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.tr: adj. 邪恶的；险恶的；不祥的
words.ex: The old house looked sinister in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 那座老房子在月光下显得阴森可怖。
words.en: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.tr:
n. 痕迹；轨迹；微量；
v. 追踪；追溯；仔细查找；
words.ex: There was no trace of blood on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 地板上没有血迹。
words.en: If you trace something such as a pattern or a shape, you draw it carefully over a piece of thin paper. You can also trace someone or something that is missing or has disappeared, by following their movements or actions.

words.ex: His sentiment about the new policy is positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对新政策的看法是积极的。
words.en: A sentiment is a thought, opinion, or idea based on a feeling about a situation, or a way of thinking about something.

words.ex: Mom reassured me that everything would be fine.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈让我安心，一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you reassure someone, you comfort them and stop them from worrying.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.ex: The team works in harmony.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队合作得很和谐。
words.en: Harmony is the pleasant combination of different notes of music played at the same time. It can also refer to a situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when things seem right or suitable together.

words.ex: The red light signifies stop.
words.ex_cn: 红灯表示停止。
words.en: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

words.ex: He testified that he saw the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他证明自己看到了那起事故。
words.en: To testify means to make a statement based on personal knowledge or belief, especially in a court of law, or to serve as evidence or proof of something's existence or truth.

words.ex: Please specify the time for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 请详细说明会议的时间。
words.en: If you specify something, you give information about what is required or should happen in a certain situation.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.tr: v. 到达…的顶点；达到高潮；告终
words.ex: The concert culminated with a loud fireworks show.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会以一场响亮的烟花表演结束。
words.en: If an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The newspaper's headline said 'City Wins Championship'.
words.ex_cn: 报纸的大字标题写着‘城市赢得冠军’。
words.en: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page.

words.tr: n. 可能发生的情况；设想；
words.ex: It's a possible scenario that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天会下雨是一个可能发生的情况。
words.en: A scenario is a description of a possible course of action or events.

words.ex: The data points correlate with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据点相互关联。
words.en: If one thing correlates with another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one thing causes the other.

words.tr:
adj. 糟糕的；可怕的；
adv. 非常；极其；
words.ex: The weather today is awful.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气很糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is awful, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, shocking, or bad.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: He is indebted to the bank for a large loan.
words.ex_cn: 他欠银行一大笔贷款。
words.en: If you say that you are indebted to someone for something, you mean that you are very grateful to them for something.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.tr: n. 公共卫生；卫生设施；
words.ex: The city improved sanitation to keep people healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了公共卫生以保障人民健康。
words.en: The conditions and processes that help maintain health and prevent disease, especially through cleanliness.

words.tr:
v. 稀释
adj. 经稀释的
words.ex: He dilutes the juice with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水稀释果汁。
words.en: To dilute a liquid means to make it thinner or weaker by adding water or another liquid to it.

words.ex: The municipal library is open every day.
words.ex_cn: 这座市政图书馆每天都开放。
words.en: Relating to a city or town or its governing body.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.ex: A dog is a mammal.
words.ex_cn: 狗是一种哺乳动物。
words.en: A mammal is a type of animal that feeds its young with milk produced by the mother's body. Mammals are warm-blooded and usually have hair or fur.

words.ex: Farmers grow grain like wheat and rice.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植小麦和大米等谷物。
words.en: A grain is a small, hard seed of a food plant such as wheat, rice, or corn, or the plant itself.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.ex: I will arrange a meeting for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我将为明天安排一次会议。
words.en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.tr:
adj. 待定的；即将发生的
prep. 在等待…期间；直到…为止
words.ex: The decision is pending.
words.ex_cn: 决定尚未做出。
words.en: If something is pending, it has not yet happened or been decided, and is often waiting for something else to happen first.

words.ex: The pendulum swings back and forth in the clock.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆在钟里来回摆动。
words.en: A pendulum is a weight that is hung from a fixed point so that it can swing freely, especially a rod with a weight at the end that regulates the mechanism of a clock.

words.tr: n. 织物；（建筑物的）结构；
words.ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是由柔软的织物制成的。
words.en: Fabric refers to cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. It can also refer to the basic structure of a building or a system.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.tr:
n. 撤退；退却；静居处；
v. 撤退；退却；
words.ex: The army ordered a retreat after the battle.
words.ex_cn: 战斗后，军队下令撤退。
words.en: If you retreat, you move away from something or someone, often because you are frightened or because you want to be alone. A retreat is also a quiet, isolated place that you go to in order to rest or to do things in private.

words.ex: The peninsula is surrounded by water on three sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个半岛三面环水。
words.en: A peninsula is a piece of land that is almost entirely surrounded by water but is connected to the mainland on one side.

words.tr: n. 玩忽职守；治疗失当；营私舞弊
words.ex: The doctor was sued for medical malpractice.
words.ex_cn: 这位医生因医疗过失被起诉。
words.en: Improper, illegal, or negligent professional activity or treatment, especially by a medical practitioner, lawyer, or public official.

words.ex: The house has a small terrace with chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个带椅子的小平台。
words.en: A terrace is a flat area of stone or grass next to a building where people can sit.

words.ex: The sequence of numbers is 1, 2, 3, 4.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的顺序是1、2、3、4。
words.en: A sequence is a set of related events, movements, or items that follow each other in a particular order.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.tr: adj. 随之发生的；作为结果的；
words.ex: The rain was heavy, and the flood was consequent.
words.ex_cn: 雨下得很大，洪水随之发生。
words.en: Following as a result or effect.

words.ex: Lying has serious consequences.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎会有严重的后果。
words.en: A consequence is a result or effect of an action or condition.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.ex: She has an extraordinary talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 她具有非凡的音乐天赋。
words.en: Something that is extraordinary is very unusual or remarkable.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
v. 使降低；使降级
n. 下坡路
words.ex: The company decided to downgrade the software version.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定将软件版本降级。
words.en: To downgrade something means to reduce its quality, value, or status.

words.tr:
v. 提升；提高；改进；
n. 增加；改进；
words.ex: He upgraded his phone to get better performance.
words.ex_cn: 他升级了手机以获得更好的性能。
words.en: To upgrade means to improve the quality or usefulness of something, or to raise it to a higher standard. It can also refer to the process of improving or raising something.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；重要的；
n. 主要产品；主要部分；主食；
words.ex: Rice is a staple food in many Asian countries.
words.ex_cn: 大米是许多亚洲国家的主要食物。
words.en: A staple is a basic food that is eaten regularly and in such quantities that it constitutes a dominant portion of a standard diet for a given people, supplying a large fraction of energy needs and generally forming a significant proportion of the intake of other nutrients as well.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.ex: He bullies his little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都欺负他的弟弟。
words.en: To bully someone means to use your strength or power to hurt or frighten them, often forcing them to do something they do not want to do.

words.tr:
adj. 暗淡的；昏暗的；模糊的
v. （使）变暗淡；（使）变模糊；（使）减弱
words.ex: The room is dim because the lights are off.
words.ex_cn: 房间很暗，因为灯关了。
words.en: If a light or a place is dim, it is not bright or is not lit very strongly.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr: v. 象征；代表；用符号表示
words.ex: The dove symbolizes peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子象征和平。
words.en: If one thing symbolizes another, it is used or regarded as a symbol of it.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: He accustoms himself to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他让自己习惯早起。
words.en: If you accustom yourself or someone else to something, you make yourself or them familiar with it or used to it.

words.ex: She coordinates the team's schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她协调团队的安排。
words.en: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it. If you coordinate the different parts of your body, you make them work together efficiently.

words.ex: He cannot comprehend the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他无法理解这个简单的数学问题。
words.en: To comprehend something means to understand it fully.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.ex: He faced ridicule for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿旧衣服而遭到嘲笑。
words.en: To ridicule someone or something means to make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.ex: He exclaim when he saw the surprise.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到惊喜时，他大喊起来。
words.en: If you exclaim, you say something suddenly and loudly, often because you are surprised, excited, or angry.

words.ex: The price of oil soared last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月石油价格骤升。
words.en: To rise or increase dramatically in amount or level.

words.ex: He staggered home after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了后摇摇晃晃地走回家。
words.en: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, as if you are about to fall.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.tr: phrase. 处理好；处置掉；除掉
words.ex: Please dispose of the trash before you leave.
words.ex_cn: 请在离开前处理好垃圾。
words.en: To get rid of something that you no longer want or need.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.tr:
n. 漠视；忽视；
v. 漠视；不理会；不顾；
words.ex: His advice was met with disregard.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议遭到了漠视。
words.en: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.ex: Mother's milk nourishes the baby.
words.ex_cn: 母乳滋养婴儿。
words.en: To nourish someone or something means to provide them with the food and other substances they need in order to live, grow, and be healthy.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.ex: The police dispersed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察驱散了人群。
words.en: If a crowd of people disperses or is dispersed, it breaks up and the people go in different directions.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: They will dismantle the old bridge next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将拆除这座旧桥。
words.en: To dismantle something means to take it to pieces.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: His opinion is subjective and not based on facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点是主观的，不是基于事实的。
words.en: Based on or influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions.

words.tr: v. 使大为震惊；使惊骇
words.ex: The accident appalled her.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故让她感到震惊。
words.en: To shock someone very much; to cause someone to feel horror or dismay.

words.ex: He felt dismay when he saw the low grade.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到低分时，感到沮丧。
words.en: Dismay is a feeling of unhappiness and disappointment.

words.tr: n. （身体或精神的）极度痛苦
words.ex: He felt deep anguish after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他感到极度痛苦。
words.en: Anguish is extreme mental suffering or physical pain.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.tr: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的
words.ex: He is complacent about his good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的好成绩感到自满。
words.en: A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.ex: He acted out of malice, not mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于恶意，而不是错误。
words.en: Malice is behavior that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.ex: The child was restless during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在漫长的会议中坐立不安。
words.en: If you are restless, you are unable to stay still or to be calm and happy, because you are bored or worried.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 考虑周到的；体贴的；
words.ex: He is considerate and always asks if others need help.
words.ex_cn: 他很体贴，总是问别人是否需要帮助。
words.en: Someone who is considerate pays attention to the needs, wishes, or feelings of other people.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He alleges that the manager stole money.
words.ex_cn: 他声称经理偷了钱。
words.en: If you allege that something bad is true, you say it but do not prove it.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: His converse was the opposite of what he said earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他的相反言论与他之前说的话相反。
words.en: To engage in conversation; to talk informally with someone.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: His greed made him steal money from his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪让他偷了朋友的钱。
words.en: Greed is the desire to have more of something, such as food or money, than is necessary or fair.

words.ex: His calm temperament helps him stay peaceful in stress.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的性情让他在压力下保持平和。
words.en: Your temperament is your basic nature, especially as it is shown in the way that you react to situations or to other people.

words.ex: This town has a peculiar custom of dancing at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有一个独特的午夜跳舞习俗。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: He criticized others for lying, but his own actions showed hypocrisy.
words.ex_cn: 他批评别人撒谎，但自己的行为却表现出虚伪。
words.en: The practice of claiming to have moral standards or beliefs to which one's own behavior does not conform; pretense.

words.ex: He is hypocritical when he says he hates lying but lies all the time.
words.ex_cn: 他说他讨厌撒谎，却总是撒谎，这很虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being hypocritical, you mean that they pretend to have qualities, beliefs, or feelings that they do not really have.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.tr: adj. 庸俗的；粗俗的；粗野的；下流的
words.ex: He used a vulgar word in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上说了一个粗俗的词。
words.en: If you describe something as vulgar, you mean that it is in bad taste or of poor quality.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.ex: Farmers use pesticide to kill insects on crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用杀虫剂来杀死作物上的昆虫。
words.en: A pesticide is a chemical substance used to kill pests, especially insects, that damage crops or are harmful to human health.

words.ex: She put a cushion on the chair to make it comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她在椅子上放了一个靠垫，让它更舒服。
words.en: A cushion is a soft bag of some ornamental material, stuffed with wool, hair, feathers, polyester staple fiber, non-woven material, or even paper torn into fragments. It may be used for sitting or kneeling upon, or to soften the hardness or angularity of a chair or couch.

words.tr: n. 化妆品；美容品；“cosmetic”的复数；
words.ex: She buys cosmetics at the drugstore.
words.ex_cn: 她在药店买化妆品。
words.en: Substances or treatments used to enhance or alter the appearance of the face or body.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.ex: He wore a funny costume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对穿了一套滑稽的服装。
words.en: A costume is a set of clothes in a style typical of a particular country or historical period, or a set of clothes worn by an actor for a particular role.

words.ex: He saw a beautiful panorama from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 他从山顶看到了美丽的全景。
words.en: A panorama is a view of a wide area, or a description or study that presents all the different parts or aspects of a particular subject.

words.ex: The reservoir provides water for the nearby town.
words.ex_cn: 这个水库为附近的城镇提供水源。
words.en: A reservoir is a large quantity of a substance that is stored and can be used when needed.

words.ex: He lives in a big mansion near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一座大宅子里。
words.en: A mansion is a very large, impressive house, especially one that is the home of a wealthy or important person.

words.ex: The pilot landed the plane safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员安全地降落了飞机。
words.en: A pilot is a person who operates the flying controls of an aircraft. Also, to pilot something means to test or introduce a new idea, product, etc., to see if it will be successful.

words.ex: The senate voted to pass the new law.
words.ex_cn: 参议院投票通过了这项新法律。
words.en: The Senate is the smaller and more important of the two parts of the parliament in some countries, for example in the United States and Australia.

words.tr: n. 习俗；习惯；关税；海关；“custom”的复数；
words.ex: In this village, it is a custom to light lanterns during the festival.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村庄，节日里点灯笼是一种习俗。
words.en: The place at a port, airport, or border where officials check the goods or luggage of people entering or leaving a country, and where they collect taxes on goods being imported.

words.ex: The people tried to overthrow the corrupt government.
words.ex_cn: 人民试图推翻腐败的政府。
words.en: To overthrow a government or a leader means to remove them from power, often by force.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr:
adj. 持不同意见的
n. 意见不同的人；持不同政见者
words.ex: The dissident spoke out against the government.
words.ex_cn: 这位持不同政见者公开反对政府。
words.en: A dissident is a person who opposes official policy, especially that of an authoritarian state.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.ex: Wheat is a basic commodity in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 小麦在许多国家是一种基本商品。
words.en: A commodity is something that is bought and sold.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.ex: The law has a loophole that lets companies avoid taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律有一个漏洞，让公司可以避税。
words.en: A loophole is a small mistake in a law or set of rules which allows people to do something that would otherwise be illegal or not allowed.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: The jury gave a guilty verdict.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团作出了有罪裁决。
words.en: A verdict is a decision made after a lot of consideration, especially one made by a jury in a court of law.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.ex: He violated the school rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: If someone violates an agreement, law, or promise, they break it.

words.ex: He has diabetes and must check his blood every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有糖尿病，必须每天检查血糖。
words.en: A medical condition in which the body cannot produce enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, leading to high levels of sugar in the blood.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.ex: The nurse will inject medicine into his arm.
words.ex_cn: 护士将把药水注入他的手臂。
words.en: To inject a substance such as a medicine or drug means to put it into someone's body using a needle and a syringe.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.ex: The soil is moist after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后土壤是潮湿的。
words.en: Slightly wet; damp or humid.

words.ex: The lab has a new apparatus for measuring temperature.
words.ex_cn: 实验室有一台新的温度测量装置。
words.en: The complex structure of a particular system or organization, or the equipment used for a specific purpose.

words.ex: He does arithmetic every day with his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他每天和妹妹一起做算术。
words.en: Arithmetic is the part of mathematics that deals with the addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of numbers.

words.ex: The rain and the thunder happened in conjunction.
words.ex_cn: 雨和雷声同时发生。
words.en: A conjunction is a word that is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.ex: He found an old manuscript in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他在图书馆里发现了一份旧手稿。
words.en: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, especially a writer's first version of a book before it is published.

words.ex: He listened to a beautiful symphony last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚听了一首美妙的交响乐。
words.en: A symphony is a long piece of music that is usually in four parts and is performed by an orchestra.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.tr: n. 事件；一集；一段经历；
words.ex: The accident was a sad episode in his life.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是他生命中的一件悲伤的事。
words.en: An episode is a part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio as one of a series, or a single event or group of related events.

words.ex: He used an analogy to explain how the heart works.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个类比来解释心脏是如何工作的。
words.en: If you make or draw an analogy between two things, you show that they are similar in some way.

words.ex: He bought a porcelain cup at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个瓷杯。
words.en: A hard, white, translucent ceramic that is made by firing a pure clay and then glazing it.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.ex: The teacher showed a specimen of a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一个蝴蝶标本。
words.en: A specimen is a single thing or example of something, especially one that is used to represent the whole group or type.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；缺乏的；有缺陷的
words.ex: The plant is deficient in sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物缺乏阳光。
words.en: If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The desert looks desolate and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠看起来荒凉而空旷。
words.en: If you describe a place as desolate, you mean that it is empty and looks sad because there are no people there or because it has been damaged.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.ex: The steam condenses into water when it touches the cold glass.
words.ex_cn: 当蒸汽接触到冷的玻璃时，会凝结成水。
words.en: If you condense something, especially a piece of writing or a speech, you make it shorter, usually by including only the most important parts.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.tr: adj. 不同寻常的；非凡的；显著的；值得注意的；
words.ex: She made a remarkable improvement in just one month.
words.ex_cn: 她在短短一个月内取得了不同寻常的进步。
words.en: Unusual or striking in a way that attracts attention.

words.ex: The restaurant serves a famous delicacy called seafood soup.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅供应一道著名的佳肴，叫海鲜汤。
words.en: Delicacy refers to the quality of being delicate, fine, or subtle in appearance, structure, or manner. It can also denote a choice or rare food item.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.ex: The company will withhold his salary until he signs the contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司会扣留他的工资，直到他签署合同。
words.en: If you withhold something that someone wants, you refuse to let them have it.

words.ex: The teacher will appraise my essay next week.
words.ex_cn: 老师下周会评价我的作文。
words.en: If you appraise something or someone, you consider them carefully and form an opinion about them.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: The doctor explained the disease in layman terms.
words.ex_cn: 医生用通俗易懂的语言解释了这种疾病。
words.en: A layman is a person who does not have specialized or professional knowledge of a subject.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: The accident caused many casualties.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了许多伤亡人员。
words.en: A casualty is a person who is killed or injured in a war or in an accident.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr: n. 一阵强劲的气流；爆炸；
words.ex: A blast of cold wind hit the window.
words.ex_cn: 一阵冷风击中了窗户。
words.en: A blast is a sudden loud noise or a strong gust of wind. It can also refer to an explosion or the act of blowing something up. As a verb, it means to explode or to criticize severely.

words.tr: n. 回路；环行；电路；巡回；
words.ex: The battery connects to the circuit to make the light work.
words.ex_cn: 电池连接到回路，使灯亮起来。
words.en: A circuit is a roughly circular line, route, or movement that starts and finishes at the same place. It can also refer to the complete path that an electric current travels along.

words.ex: He acted on impulse and bought the car.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动买了那辆车。
words.en: An impulse is a sudden strong desire to do something without thinking about the consequences.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is marvelous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色极好。
words.en: If you describe something as marvelous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good.

words.ex: They placed a memorial at the site of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他们在事故地点放置了一座纪念物。
words.en: A memorial is a structure or event established to remind people of a person or event.

words.ex: The tree has many colorful ornaments.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树上有许多彩色的装饰品。
words.en: An ornament is an object that is used to make something look more attractive but is usually considered to have no practical purpose.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.ex: Wear a helmet as a precaution when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔作为一种预防措施。
words.en: A precaution is an action that is intended to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.ex: We had a snack and some drinks as refreshment after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后，我们吃了点心和喝了一些饮料作为茶点。
words.en: Refreshment refers to the act of refreshing or the state of being refreshed, especially by food or drink. It can also mean a light meal or drinks served in a social setting.

words.ex: The farm has a surplus of apples this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年农场苹果过剩。
words.en: A surplus is an amount of something that is extra or more than what is needed.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: He put his clothes in the wardrobe.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服放进衣橱里。
words.en: A wardrobe is a tall cupboard or cabinet in which you can hang your clothes.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr:
n. 回想
v. 回想
words.ex: In retrospect, I should have studied harder.
words.ex_cn: 回顾过去，我本该更努力学习的。
words.en: When you consider something in retrospect, you think about it afterwards, and often have a different opinion about it from the one that you had at the time.

words.ex: The fireworks at night were a beautiful spectacle.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的烟花是一场美丽的奇观。
words.en: A spectacle is a visually striking performance or display.

words.tr: n. 迷信；迷信观念（或思想）；
words.ex: He avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迷信而不愿从梯子下走过。
words.en: A superstition is a belief or practice resulting from ignorance, fear of the unknown, trust in magic or chance, or a false conception of causation.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: The test results confirm he has the disease.
words.ex_cn: 检测结果证实他患有这种疾病。
words.en: To confirm something means to establish its truth or validity by providing evidence or proof.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.tr:
adj. 古老的；
n. 古董；
words.ex: He bought an antique chair from the old market.
words.ex_cn: 他从旧市场买了一把古老的椅子。
words.en: Something that is antique is old and often valuable because it is rare or well made.

words.ex: He is a veteran player with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位经验丰富的老练球员。
words.en: A veteran is someone who has a lot of experience in a particular field or activity, especially in the armed forces.

words.tr:
v. 摔跤；扭斗；奋力对付
n. 摔跤；角力；扭斗
words.ex: He tries to wrestle the dog away from the trash.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把狗从垃圾桶旁拉开。
words.en: To engage in a physical contest, typically involving grappling and trying to throw or immobilize the opponent, or to struggle with a difficult problem or decision.

words.tr: n. 保证；保修单；保证书
words.ex: The phone comes with a one-year warranty.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一年的保修期。
words.en: A warranty is a written guarantee, often given to the purchaser of an article by its manufacturer, promising to repair or replace it if necessary within a specified period of time.

words.tr: n. 仔细研究；详细检查；
words.ex: The teacher examined the student's work under close scrutiny.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作业进行了仔细研究。
words.en: If someone or something is under scrutiny, they are being studied or observed very carefully.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.tr: n. 影响；方位；轴承；举止； v. 忍受；“bear”的现在分词；
words.ex: The new policy has a big bearing on our daily lives.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对我们日常生活有很大影响。
words.en: The manner in which one conducts or carries oneself, including posture and gestures; also refers to a machine part that supports another part and reduces friction.

words.tr: adj. 高的；崇高的；傲慢的
words.ex: The mountain has a lofty peak.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个很高的山顶。
words.en: If you say that someone behaves in a lofty way, you are critical of them for behaving in a proud and rather unpleasant way, as if they think they are very important.

words.ex: The boy tried to seize the ball.
words.ex_cn: 男孩试图抓住球。
words.en: If you seize something, you take hold of it quickly, firmly, and forcefully.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.ex: He possesses a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有一栋靠近湖边的小房子。
words.en: If you possess something, you have it or own it.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.ex: The remote needs a new battery.
words.ex_cn: 遥控器需要新电池。
words.en: A battery is a device that produces electricity to provide power for radios, cars, toys, etc.

words.ex: He was a pioneer in space exploration.
words.ex_cn: 他是太空探索的先驱者。
words.en: A pioneer is someone who is one of the first people to do something that others will later develop or continue. Pioneers are also people who are among the first to go to live in a new area, especially in the past when people were trying to settle in new lands.

words.tr: n. 代码；编码；行为准则；密码；法典；
words.ex: He wrote a simple code to solve the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一段简单的代码来解决这个数学问题。
words.en: A code is a system of words, letters, figures, or other symbols substituted for other words, letters, etc., especially for the purposes of secrecy. As a verb, it means to convert (a message or other information) into a code.

words.ex: He can decode the secret message.
words.ex_cn: 他能译解这个秘密信息。
words.en: To convert coded data into intelligible form.

words.tr:
n. 树桩；残段；残根
v. 难倒；重步走
words.ex: The tree stump is still in the yard.
words.ex_cn: 树桩还在院子里。
words.en: A stump is the base part of a tree that remains after the rest of the tree has been cut down. It can also refer to a difficult problem or to the act of walking heavily.

words.ex: This tradition originates from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统起源于古代。
words.en: To originate means to have a specific beginning or to start something.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.
